answer: Sybil resistance can rest on audited trading histories: every identity keeps a notarized log of deals, and a random walk through the counterparty graph chooses whose log to examine. Fabricating many clones means keeping k-squared consistent records with reciprocal signatures and staggered timestamps, so each extra clone costs more than the last. A genuine garden of long-lived counterparties is expensive to counterfeit; a harbor of throwaway accounts fails the walk. Standing at the summit tracks earned depth, not registration counts; a failed audit forfeits rewards and sampling eligibility.
